summary: SSE disconnect during large inline image embed truncates markdown image tag and leaves broken media on resume
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed that long responses which embed an inline image (markdown ![alt](data:image/png;base64,....)) are truncated when an SSE disconnect occurs mid-stream. On resume the client receives a stream that ends with a broken markdown image tag (missing closing parenthesis) and the rendered output in the customer's app shows a broken image.

Impact:
- Affects a subset of long streaming responses that include inline base64 image blobs or very long image URLs.
- Customer-visible content corruption: broken markdown image tags and missing embedded images.
- Occurred intermittently for customer sessions behind a corporate proxy during a short transient network blip; customer reports this happened ~3 times in the last 24h across multiple users.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod, us-east region, public API.
- Customer: Polaris Assist (self_serve).
- Model: open-chat-7B-v1.

Steps to reproduce (attempted):
1) Create a prompt that instructs the model to include a small inline image as a base64 data URI in markdown (example: ![diagram](data:image/png;base64,<long-payload>)).
2) Start SSE streaming request with client that supports resume tokens.
3) During large payload emission (image blob chunking), force a short disconnect at the edge (we tested by dropping the connection on a local reverse proxy).
4) Reconnect/resume session.
5) Observe the final assembled stream on the client — in failing cases the closing ")" of the image markdown and the tail of the base64 payload are missing.

Observed logs / traces:
- Edge proxy (customer side) shows TCP FIN and immediate reconnect within ~2s.
- Load balancer logs: upstream returned 200 OK then connection close; no 5xx.
- Serving runtime trace (request-id: req-20260312-9a2b): last sent SSE chunk ends inside a base64 data URI; resume window applied new chunks but server-side resume framing omitted last buffer flush.
- Client console shows lastChunk: "!...data:image/png;base64,AAA..." (truncated), parsing error when client attempts to decode.

Hypothesis / initial analysis:
- When SSE chunk boundaries fall inside a large token (base64 blob), our streaming resume logic sometimes fails to emit a final flush of the pending buffer for that token after a reconnect race.
- The edge-proxy or client reconnect sequence may result in the server replaying only up to the last committed resume offset; the final partial buffer that contains the closing parenthesis is lost if it was not checkpointed.
- The issue surfaces more often with very large inline payloads (image data URIs) than with plain text because chunk boundaries split binary-like base64 runs and the parser on the client expects a complete markdown token.

Workarounds / mitigation attempted:
- Advised customer to avoid embedding base64 images inline in streaming responses; instead provide a signed URL returned after generation. Customer confirmed this avoids the corruption.
- We tested forcing more frequent resume checkpoints on a staging runtime and saw reduced occurrence, but this is not yet safe for prod without load testing.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering (Serving-Runtime) to add unit test that simulates streaming a large base64 data URI with mid-stream disconnect and validate final flush semantics. (Assigned: @ethan-zhao)
- Short-term: add conservative flush on resume boundary in the edge proxy path to ensure any pending chunk is emitted to the client (hotfix candidate).
- Product: update streaming resume guidance in docs to warn about large inline media in streaming responses.
- Support: notify Polaris Assist of recommended pattern (use upload-to-storage + link) and provide ETA for fix.

Resolution notes (in progress):
- Reproducer built in staging that consistently hits the condition when chunk size set to 8KB and the base64 payload spans multiple chunks.
- Patch candidate under review that ensures resume triggers buffer flush-of-current-token; still measuring performance impact.
